observation.visible_scene: A dark indoor concert/festival arena viewed from the audience side. A central stage light source sits low in the middle of the frame, from which numerous thin laser beams (red, white, and green/yellow) radiate outward in fan-like and criss-crossing patterns against a black background. A horizontal overhead truss beam runs across the top, a vertical support pole stands on the right, a camera-on-tripod silhouette sits at the left foreground, and a dense crowd silhouette fills the bottom. Two rectangular video screens flank the stage (left and right). The whole scene is punctuated by repeated, very bright white strobe washes that briefly flood the arena, revealing stage haze/smoke and the crowd.
visible_changes: Laser beam configuration and color evolve over time: early frames (1-3) are dominated by red beams fanning upward; mid frames (9-12, 15-22) shift to predominantly white beams forming wider fans and zigzag/'M'-like crossing patterns; later frames (24-41) mix white/green fans with red beams concentrated at the base.

Periodic white strobe flashes occur at several points (e.g. frames 4, 13, 23, 32, 37, 40), each momentarily overexposing the center, washing out the beams, and illuminating the crowd and atmospheric haze before the scene returns to the darker laser-only look.
The side video screens change content: showing green fan/line graphics in some frames (e.g. 9, 17, 24) and red/orange imagery in others (e.g. 25-31, 33-39).
The crowd silhouette and foreground camera rig remain present throughout, becoming clearly visible only during the bright strobe moments.

Beam origins and the overhead truss, right pole, and stage center stay in essentially the same image positions across frames, indicating the light patterns change in place rather than the viewpoint translating.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or cue for each strobe flash and the overall show structure are not visible.
What precedes the first frame and follows the last frame (the segment is a mid-show crop).
Audio, performer identity, and full stage layout beyond the lit center are unseen.
uncertain_details: Any camera movement is minimal/uncertain; the fixed truss and pole suggest a near-static shot with possible slight handheld jitter rather than deliberate panning.
Whether the bright washes are strobes, stage lighting, or a combination cannot be distinguished from the frames alone.
Exact beam geometry between sampled frames is unknown due to the 0.1s sampling.
